simple.meaning: מַתָּת (mattâth) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a present.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at 1 Kings 13:7. The surrounding context includes offering, kingship.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מַתָּת (H4991) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: מַתָּת (mattâth) / H4991 is traced through 1 Kings 13:7, Proverbs 25:14, Ecclesiastes 3:13, Ecclesiastes 5:18 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H4991. mattath [ מַתַּת ] noun feminine id.; — absolute מַתָּ֑ת 1Kin 13:7 ; construct מַתַּת Prov 25:14 4 t.; — gift = reward 1Kin 13:7 ; יָדוֺ מַתַּת the gift of his hand , i.e. of his power, what he is able to give Ezek 46:5 , 11 (compare מַתָּנָה and יָד 2 ); ׳מ אֱלֹהִים Eccl 3:13 the gift of God (of the enjoyment of man), so 5:18 ; ׳מ שָׁ֑קֶר Prov 25:14 a gift of falsity , i.e. one promised and not given.
